Series::extract_put_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::extract_put_(pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec> specs, const Series& values) -> Series&

What It Does¶

Writes into the current series through the full ExtractSpec selector language, mutates in place, and returns *this.

This is the write-side counterpart to extract(). If traverse_put_() is the strict “only write through a plain view” surface, extract_put_() is the broader surface that accepts selectors requiring materialization: reverse slices, boolean masks, integer index series, and mixed selector forms.

The mental model is:

  • extract() selects values

  • extract_put_() selects destinations

  • the selected destinations are then filled from values

Internally, non-trivial selectors are normalized into explicit index series and the final update is routed through index_put_(). That is why this method can write through selector shapes that are not representable as a simple chained view.

Parameters¶

specs (pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>)

The destination selector.

This method accepts the same broad selector language documented on extract(), including:

  • scalar integer indices

  • SliceAll()

  • bounded and unbounded slice ranges

  • negative-step slices

  • boolean mask series

  • integer index series

  • Ellipsis

  • NewAxis

Important details:

  • Scalar indices consume one source axis and target a narrower destination.

  • Identity slices preserve the full addressed axis.

  • Negative-step slices are legal here, even though they are rejected by traverse_put_().

  • Boolean and integer advanced selectors are legal here.

  • NewAxis is accepted for selector compatibility, but it does not create a new writable axis. It is ignored for destination addressing because it consumes no source dimension.

values (const Series&)

The source data to assign into the selected destination positions.

values follows two cardinality rules:

  • If values.numel() == 1, it broadcasts across the full selection.

  • Otherwise values.numel() must equal the selected element count exactly.

Before writing, values is converted to the destination platform and dtype if needed. Matching is by element count, not by preserving the original shape of values; non-scalar sources are flattened to the selected logical order before the write is applied.

Returns¶

Series& The same series, after mutation.

Examples¶

Example 1. A scalar source broadcasts across an entire selected column.

auto grid = pluss::make_series(
    std::vector<double>{10, 11, 12, 13, 20, 21, 22, 23, 30, 31, 32, 33},
    {3, 4});

const std::vector<ExtractSpec> fill_column{
    pluss::Slicing::SliceAll(),
    std::int64_t{1}};

grid.extract_put_(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(fill_column),
    pluss::codem::value(-1.0));

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[10, -1, 12, 13],
  [20, -1, 22, 23],
  [30, -1, 32, 33]]

This is the simplest successful case: the selector names three destination positions, and a scalar source is replicated into each one.

Example 2. A reverse slice is legal here, so the write follows the selector’s logical visitation order rather than physical storage order.

const std::vector<ExtractSpec> reverse_write{
    std::int64_t{1},
    pluss::Slicing::SliceRange(-1, pluss::Slicing::Slice::kUnbounded, -2)};

auto reverse_values = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{90, 70}, {2});

grid.extract_put_(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(reverse_write),
    reverse_values);

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[10, -1, 12, 13],
  [20, 70, 22, 90],
  [30, -1, 32, 33]]

The selector visits row 1, columns 3 then 1. The two source elements are consumed in exactly that order, so 90 lands in column 3 and 70 lands in column 1.

Example 3. NewAxis may appear in the selector, but it does not add a new writeable destination dimension.

const std::vector<ExtractSpec> with_newaxis{
    pluss::Slicing::NewAxis(),
    pluss::Slicing::SliceAll(),
    std::int64_t{0}};

auto first_col = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{100, 200, 300}, {3});

grid.extract_put_(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(with_newaxis),
    first_col);

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[100, -1, 12, 13],
  [200, 70, 22, 90],
  [300, -1, 32, 33]]

Semantically this still means “write into column 0 of every row.” NewAxis does not create a phantom target axis that values must somehow match.

Example 4. Non-scalar sources must match the selected element count exactly.

try {
  const std::vector<ExtractSpec> mismatch_specs{
      std::int64_t{0},
      pluss::Slicing::SliceRange(0, 4, 2)};

  auto mismatch_values = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{1, 2, 3}, {3});

  grid.extract_put_(
      pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(mismatch_specs),
      mismatch_values);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

Series::extract_put_: source must be scalar or match selected element count

The selector picks only two destination positions, so a three-element replacement series is invalid.

Notes¶

  • extract_put_() is the richest selector-write surface on Series.

  • If the selector is naturally view-like and you want that restriction enforced up front, prefer traverse_put_().

  • If you want the same selector power without mutating the current object, use extract_put().

  • For flat or explicit index-list writes, index_put_() can be more direct, but for most readable N-D region writes extract_put_() is the clearer API.

See Also¶

  • Series::extract_put: same selector language, but returns a modified copy.

  • Series::traverse_put_: stricter write surface that accepts only view-representable selectors.

  • Series::extract: read through the same selector language.

  • Series::index_put_: explicit index-list writes.
